messages:
Priya: quick async — after yesterday's deploy we need to lock the next 2-week slice. primary decision: stabilize (bugs) vs polish (UX/perf). proposing 60% bugs / 40% polish. thoughts?
Liam: +1 on 60/40. engineering capacity next sprint: ~6 devs, but 1 is blocked by infra work for Dedicated autoscale.
Ava: QA list of P0s (short): streaming drop on long sessions, embedding drift on model-v2, intermittent retry loop causing doubled tokens. all reproducible in staging.
Marcus: from infra: the memory leak on cuda-rt shows up under heavy batching. fix is non-trivial (~3-4d) but removes a weekly slick incident.
Sami: product note — two Named accounts (Enterprise) hit the streaming bug in prod yesterday; CS flagged for risk of escalation.
Dora (Design): polish items are mostly microcopy and flow fixes for streaming UI + a smoother reconnect UX. low dev cost, high perceived quality.
Ella (CS): customers asking for better visibility into fallbacks: a per-session metric + clearer error messaging would reduce support tickets. that counts for polish but has clear CS ROI.
Priya: here's a quick rubric I used to score backlog candidates:
```
impact = (#customers_affected * severity_weight)
cost = dev_days + infra_risk_score
priority = impact / max(1,cost)
```
Priya: Using that, top 5 this morning: streaming drop (impact 90), memory leak (impact 60), embedding drift (impact 50), streaming reconnect UX (impact 30), token billing edge-case (impact 20).
Liam: estimate check: streaming drop = 5 dev-days; memory leak = 7 dev-days; embedding drift = 2 dev-days; reconnect UX = 2 dev-days; billing edge-case = 1 dev-day.
Marcus: infra prefers memory leak as highest technical debt, but it doesn't surface for all customers. if we don't fix it, we hit 1 major incident/month.
Sami: I'd prioritize streaming drop for immediate fix (customer escalations) and ship reconnect UX as quick polish in parallel. that maps to a 50/50 split practically.
Ava: ETA: if we allocate two devs to streaming drop and one to reconnect UX+tests we can close both in 10 business days.
Priya: decision proposal: sprint A (next 2 weeks): 1) block on streaming drop (P0) + reconciliation tests, 2) ship reconnect UX & copy, 3) schedule memory leak deep-fix for sprint B (requires infra window).
Liam: agree. put memory leak on the radar for sprint B — we should reserve a 2-day on-call window for rollout validation.
Dora (Design): I'll drop UX copy + tiny animations in a single PR. need 1 review from Eng.
Ella (CS): I'll prepare a customer note template and proactive outreach list for the affected accounts once we have a fix branch.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: hotfix/streaming-p0 -> staging (sha 8f3a2c) — CI passing.
Priya: cool — action items: Liam assign owners for streaming and reconnect, Marcus schedule infra window for memory leak, Dora + Ava pair on tests, Ella prepare comms. I'll update roadmap board and scope doc.
Liam: assigned. I'll also add a rollback plan and quick canary checklist:
```
- canary traffic: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 2h
- monitor: error-rate, tail-latency, token-duplication
- rollback: revert deploy, clear KV cache
```
Priya: thanks all — we'll re-check in async in ~36h and do a short sync if any blocker pops. :thumbsup:
Sami: thanks — agree with plan. leaning to keep memory leak as sprint B priority but flag it in product notes.
Ava: noted, will add test cases and update the regression suite.
Marcus: scheduling infra window now.
Ella: prepping customer outreach template.
Priya: closing thread; I'll post updated board and add links to tickets: https://tracker/INF-542, https://tracker/INF-548.
